subject: Next step: Dedicated pool sizing call for FinLytics
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Selena Ortiz <selena@finlytics.io>
Cc: Adam Chen <adam@finlytics.io>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + proposed dedicated-pool sizing call

Hi Selena / Adam,

Thanks again for the discovery earlier today — really helpful to understand the FinLytics inference footprint and the product constraints. Quick recap and proposal for next steps so we can size a dedicated pool that meets your latency and throughput goals.

Recap from our call:
- Primary workload: document summarization + redaction pipelines (internal and partner-facing).
- Current model family: a 13B open model variant for eval.
- Key goals: predictable p95 latency, stable throughput during batch and burst windows, and data isolation.

To make the dedicated-sizing call productive, could you confirm the following before we meet? I've attached a short questionnaire (finlytics-dedicated-sizing-questionnaire.pdf) you can fill in or just paste answers in a reply:
1) Sustained requests/sec (or requests/min) and typical peak concurrency.
2) Average input tokens and expected output tokens per request.
3) Desired latency SLO (p95 target).
4) Any networking/K8s restrictions (eg: VPC peering, egress limits).
5) Preferred model(s) or tolerance for quantized variants.

Proposed times for a 60-minute dedicated pool sizing & technical deep-dive (PT):
- Thu Jul 23: 10:00–11:00 or 14:00–15:00
- Fri Jul 24: 09:30–10:30 or 11:30–12:30

If you prefer, pick a slot and I will send a calendar invite. I recommend inviting your infra lead (Adam) and any SRE folks so we can align on networking and monitoring needs.

Attaching: finlytics-dedicated-sizing-questionnaire.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192
From: Selena Ortiz <selena@finlytics.io>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Adam Chen <adam@finlytics.io>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + proposed dedicated-pool sizing call

Hi Olga — thanks for the clear recap. Adam and I talked and we can do Fri Jul 24 09:30 PT. Adam will also invite our SRE (cc'd).

Quick answers to the questionnaire (high level):
- Sustained: ~200 requests/min (averaged across our worker fleet).
- Peak concurrency: ~40 concurrent requests during business hour spikes (roughly 11:00–13:00 PT).
- Tokens: input ~220 tokens, output ~140 tokens on average.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 800ms for core summarization endpoint, best-effort for lower-priority batch jobs.
- Networking: VPC peering is required; egress IP allowlist will be needed.
- Models: evaluating 13B family; open to quantized 13B if latency improves without regression.

We can share a smaller set of traces and a sample payload ahead of the call if helpful. See you Friday 09:30 PT.

Best,
Selena
Product Lead, FinLytics
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Selena Ortiz <selena@finlytics.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Adam Chen <adam@finlytics.io>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Confirmed: Fri Jul 24 09:30 PT — Dedicated sizing deep-dive

Perfect — thanks for the details, Selena. I've penciled in Fri Jul 24 at 09:30 PT and sent a calendar invite (link below).

Pre-call notes / ask for the FinLytics team (will make the session higher bandwidth):
- If you can, paste or attach a 1–2 minute synthetic request trace (one representative payload) and a brief QPS/day snapshot.
- If there are multiple endpoints with different SLAs, flag them in the doc or in the invite.
- Confirm the model variant you prefer us to evaluate (exact HF repo or manifest).

Agenda (60m):
1) Quick alignment on objectives and constraints (10m)
2) Review provided traces & traffic shape (15m)
3) Throughput/latency modeling and pool sizing options (25m)
4) Rollout/observability and next steps (10m)

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pool-brief.pdf (high-level sizing approach)
Calendar invite: https://calendar.redwood.com/meet/olga/finlytics-sizing
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/RDW-2026-074

Dev — looping you in to lead the technical sizing on our side. Marissa — wanted you on the invite for commercial context.

Thanks,
Olga
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Selena Ortiz <selena@finlytics.io>, Adam Chen <adam@finlytics.io>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Pre-call checklist + what I'll bring to the sizing session

Hi Selena / Adam / Olga — looking forward to the 09:30 PT call. A few quick items I'll bring and request to keep the meeting focused: 

What I'll bring (on Redwood side):
- Estimated recommended GPU pool configurations for a 13B-era model given the traffic you described (sustained vs burst lanes).
- Rough latency/throughput curves for a 13B quantized vs FP16 run (p50/p95 estimates).
- Options for autoscale + burst capacity and expected cost tradeoffs.

What would be helpful from FinLytics before/during the call:
- One representative request and one representative "heavy" request (JSON).
- Recent logs or a CSV with requests/sec by 5m bucket for the last two business days (if available).
- Any internal CPU/GPU affinity or network constraints for your VPC environment.

If you prefer to drop documents ahead of time, reply to this thread or upload to the HubSpot deal we linked. Otherwise we can work through samples live.

See you at 09:30 PT — I'll share a short sizing slide during the call and record the session notes.

— Dev
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
